Labour economics

Labour economics studies how workers and firms make decisions about employment, wages, skills, and job search. It also examines institutions such as labour regulations, unions, contracts, and social protection.

The subject provides tools for understanding unemployment, wage differences, migration, human capital, labour supply, and employer behaviour. These topics are closely connected to development and public policy.
